meta.description: Simulation study for 'Where Does Criticism End?' (synthetic data only; no real survey data).
meta.experiment_names: Experiments are labelled X1-X9 (X1b, X2b). X1-X5 were labelled E1-E5 (E1b) in the first run of 2026-11-03 and were renamed on 2026-11-03 to avoid a clash with the estimands (E1)-(E9) of sec:design-estimands; their seeds (experiment indices 1-5), configurations and results are unchanged. Mapping: E1->X1, E1b->X1b, E2->X2, E3->X3, E4->X4, E5->X5.
meta.seed_scheme: numpy SeedSequence([base_seed, experiment_index, cell keys..., rep])
meta.code_sha256_16_note: per experiment: experiments.<E>.code_sha256_16 (hashes of the code that produced it)
meta.estimation: Limited-information: two-step polychoric correlations (Olsson 1979) with influence-function asymptotic covariance; DWLS fit (diagonal weights) of the bifactor model in the IRT (theta) parameterisation; sandwich SEs; nonparametric bootstrap for ECV intervals.

X1.description: Recovery of loadings, item-level ECV, boundary set (tau=0.5) and S-I correlation; single group, bifactor DGP (probit GRM), DWLS on polychorics, bootstrap percentile and logit-Wald (sandwich) 95% intervals.
X1.seeds: data: SeedSequence([base, 1, cfg_index, n, rep]).spawn(2)[0]; bootstrap: .spawn(2)[1]

X1b.description: As X1 for a design close to proportionality (rem:id-heterogeneity): S-block ECVs 0.65-0.75 (common communality 0.55), n_I = 3, so Assumption id-het holds only weakly in S and fails in I.

X2.description: Two groups (n=1500 each), DIF on Israel-related items I1, I2 (uniform) and I3 (non-uniform); focal-group latent means (G,S,I) = (0.3, 0, 0.3); strategies: naive (full invariance), oracle (true DIF items free), free-baseline with anchor sets (correct, contam1, contam2) and the pre-registered procedure (Wald + BH q=0.05 + expected-score effect size >= 0.25, then refit); stereotype-only anchors S1-S4 with mu_I, sigma_I fixed (rem:id-anchor-S). Naive = concurrent calibration with equal group sizes (rem:id-concurrent). Focal ECV per def:boundary (with focal factor variances).
X2.seeds: SeedSequence([base, 2, round(100 kappa), rep]); population weights: [base, 2, 999, round(100 kappa)]

summary_recomputed.note: summary recomputed from raw/E2.json with the code hashed here; the replications themselves were produced by the code in code_sha256_16

X3.description: One sensitive item, threshold-shift model of social desirability (def:le-shift, normal ogive): pi = 0.30, pi^D = 0.20 (SDB = 0.10) unless false endorsement phi > 0. Part A: split design, equal vs Neyman (thm:design(a)) vs pilot plug-in allocation; SDB_S (eq:le-split) and a covariate-adjusted version. Part B: paired design (thm:joint-sdb(b),(c)), post-stratified SDB_PS and combined eta-hat, under monotonicity (phi = 0) and false endorsement (phi = 0.02), vs the split design. Part C: control-list menu J in 2..6, binary within-pair correlation rho in {0, -0.6}, floor/ceiling probability kc = kf in {0, 0.5} (thm:design(c),(d)).

X4.description: MRP of the area mean of G (50 areas, 32 demographic cells per area, differential non-response by age and education); score y = theta_G + N(0, s_m^2) (conditionally unbiased); MRP = REML random-intercept model on y + poststratification (eq:mrp), which in this Gaussian setting is the latent regression with measurement error integrated out; two-step EAP = the same MRP on posterior-mean scores under one common prior (prop:eap); direct = area sample mean (unweighted and national cell-weighted). A new population is drawn in every replication.

X5.description: Population index P(agree with >= k of 8 S items) by group vs the latent mean difference delta of G; random uniform DIF b_j^(1) = b_j^(0) + N(0, s^2) sd_j on the S items; reversal = sign(index difference) != sign(delta). Exact (quadrature) for 1000 random configurations per (s, |delta|); finite-sample check with n = 1000 per group.
X5.seeds: SeedSequence([base, 5, round(100 s), round(100 |delta|)]); finite sample [base, 5, 500 + round(100 s), round(100 delta), rep]

X2b.description: As X2 (two groups of 1500, focal latent means (0.3, 0, 0.3)), with ideology-type uniform DIF on two of the four stereotype anchors (S1, S2: thresholds lowered by kappa_S latent-response SDs in the focal group), with (kappa_I = 0.4) or without (kappa_I = 0) the X2 DIF on I1-I3. Strategies: oracle (all DIF-free items as anchors), default anchors S1-S4, I5, I6 (free baseline, and the revised BH-only screen + refit), stereotype-only anchors S1-S4 (mu_I, sigma_I fixed). Leave-one-anchor-out spread of mu_G for both anchor sets. Population: probability limits and the first-order bias and bound eq:id-anchor-bound with W the efficient information of the anchors' focal intercepts for the DWLS estimator.
X2b.seeds: SeedSequence([base, 22, round(100 kappa_I), round(100 kappa_S), rep]); population weights: [base, 22, 999, round(100 kappa_I), round(100 kappa_S)]

summary_recomputed.note: summary recomputed from raw/X2b.json with the code hashed here; the replications themselves were produced by the code in code_sha256_16

X6.description: Directional misspecifications at the registered sizes (10 S, 8 ID, 6 IT items; n = 6000; probit GRM, five categories). (a) the trope-based items IT1-IT6 cross-load on S with standardised loading c; (b) an acquiescence (random-intercept) factor with slope alpha, +alpha on positively worded and -alpha on reverse-keyed items, with the registered keying (4 reverse-keyed items: S2, S7, ID2, ID6) or balanced keying (half of each block), and one cell with item-specific acquiescence slopes (0.5-1.5 alpha). True ECVs are the content ECVs a_G^2/(a_G^2 + a_s^2) of the item's own domain. Fitted: the standard bifactor model (bif); with free cross-loadings of IT on S (cross); with a one-parameter acquiescence factor using the instrument's keying (mf); refit with I = ID only (ipo); and a two-stage rule that uses cross when the one-sided IT x S mean-residual test rejects at 5% (twostage); and the plan's check (BH q = 0.05 over the 60 IT x S residual correlations, a one-item cross-loading model for each IT item in turn; a flagged item is classified only if the primary model and its G share in the one-item model agree). Classification: Bonferroni logit-Wald intervals over the Israel-related items (the plan's rule).
X6.seeds: SeedSequence([base, 6, cell_index, rep]).spawn(2): data, starts; population weights [base, 6, 999, cell_index]

X7.description: The revised DIF screen of sec:design-groups run end to end on the X2 data sets (same seeds): free-baseline fit with the anchor set, Wald test of each non-anchor item, Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05, every BH-significant item freed (no effect-size requirement), partial-invariance refit. The expected-score difference averaged over the focal latent distribution is recorded as the secondary description (small DIF if < 0.25).
X7.seeds: the X2 data sets: SeedSequence([base, 2, round(100 kappa), rep])

X8.description: Identification of the threshold shift delta_j by a list experiment (prop:list-irt(b),(c)). X1 six-item bank, sensitive item I4 (ECV 0.60), agreement = top two categories; two groups (theta ~ N(mu_x, I), mu_1 = (0.5, 0, 0.3)) of 3000, each randomised to direct, list-control and list-treatment arms (1/3 each); J = 4 controls in two pairs with rho = -0.6. The two-group bifactor model is fitted to the direct arm with I4 free across groups; delta_x solves eq:le-irt-root in each group. Cells: common uniform shift 0.4 SD; group-specific shifts 0.4 and 0.8 SD; non-uniform private response (slope x 0.5, prop:list-irt-ext). Test of a common shift: z-test of delta_1 = delta_0.

X9.description: Tests of within-domain heterogeneity (asm:id-het; rule D2(ii)) at the registered sizes (10 S items, 14 I items). Per domain: the joint Wald test of a non-redundant set of |D|(|D|-3)/2 polychoric tetrads (null: all tetrads vanish, i.e. id-het fails); the residual-based one-factor test (Browne 1984) of the same null; the intersection-union test (reject iff the joint test rejects for every D minus one item); and the earlier rule (any of the 3,633 within-domain tetrads significant after Bonferroni). Configurations: proportional (null), all but one proportional (null), all but two proportional with the two on a second line, near-proportional, and the registered heterogeneous bank.
